title: The Museum Power Failure
incident: During a planned 10-minute electrical substation transfer at 2:00 AM, a gold Minoan ceremonial dagger disappeared from an alarmed display case. The backup lighting operated as intended, but the gallery infrared laser grid deactivated 4 minutes earlier than the scheduled maintenance window.
centralQuestions: Why did the infrared laser grid fail 4 minutes ahead of schedule at 1:56 AM?
Who had access to the master electrical transfer junction?
Did the muddy shoeprint match the maintenance staff or a visitor who hid after hours?

timeline.event: Electrician Ronald Vance signs into basement electrical distribution vault.
Laser alarm grid on Case 4 drops offline (4 minutes early).
Planned substation transfer begins; main lights extinguish, emergency halogen lights turn on.
Patrol guard notices Case 4 display glass lifted and dagger missing.

suspects.name: Ronald Vance
suspects.motive: Severe tax arrears; threatened with home foreclosure.
suspects.statement: He says the early laser drop was caused by an unexpected relay surge on Panel B.
relevant_evidence: He controlled the Panel B breaker switches.
supporting_evidence: Panel B shows signs of electrical thermal stress.
suspicious_evidence: His multimeter had copper shavings matching the laser grid fuse terminals.
suspects.uncertainty: Copper shavings are common in electrical service bags.
open_questions: Did he cut the laser grid intentionally at 1:56 AM?

suspects.name: Dr. Beatrice Ramos
suspects.motive: Convinced the dagger was looted illegally from Greece and belongs in a repatriation trust.
suspects.statement: She says she was in her office reviewing catalog entries.
relevant_evidence: Her office is located directly above Gallery Room 2.
supporting_evidence: Office terminal logged active keystrokes until 1:50 AM.
suspicious_evidence: Glass lifters in her office had fresh suction ring marks matching the Case 4 vitrine.
suspects.uncertainty: Curators frequently use suction lifters during exhibition rotation.
open_questions: Did she leave her office between 1:50 and 2:10 AM?

suspects.name: Garrick Cole
suspects.motive: Offered $50,000 payoff by private antiquities syndicate.
suspects.statement: He says he was on the ground floor monitoring emergency perimeter doors.
relevant_evidence: His patrol wand was swiped at Station 4 (Gallery Room) at 1:58 AM.
Footprint near case matches his combat boot tread.
suspicious_evidence: Station 4 wand swipe was 2 minutes after the laser grid died.
suspects.uncertainty: Guards are supposed to inspect galleries when alarms or power anomalies occur.
open_questions: Was his 1:58 AM presence routine patrol or theft execution?

witnesses.name: Relief Guard Timothy
witnesses.statement: I saw Dr. Ramos walking in the corridor around 1:52 AM carrying a cloth roll.
witnesses.limitations: Could not see inside the cloth roll.

evidence.title: Relay Panel B Fuse Tampering
evidence.description: The fuse controlling the laser grid was manually bridged with a jumper wire at 1:56 AM, bypassing the main relay.
evidence.establishes: The laser grid drop at 1:56 AM was deliberate sabotage, not an accidental power surge.

evidence.title: Patrol Wand Timestamp
evidence.description: Garrick Cole's security key wand touched Reader #4 at 1:58 AM, exactly between the laser sabotage and planned outage.
evidence.establishes: Cole was physically standing beside Case 4 while the lasers were disabled.
evidence.does_not_establish: That Cole lifted the vitrine glass.

evidence.title: Vitrine Suction Ring Marks
evidence.description: Dual 4-inch rubber suction marks found on the exterior case glass matching Ramos's specialized German glass lifters.
evidence.establishes: Case 4 was lifted using Ramos's exact suction lifters.

evidence.title: Emergency Breaker Override Pin
evidence.description: Substation electrical panel #2 contained a bypassed magnetic breaker peg causing the secondary auxiliary lights to delay ignition by 90 seconds.
evidence.establishes: The blackout duration in the antiquities hall was intentionally prolonged.
evidence.reliability_notes: Insulated wire fragment recovered from panel.

evidence.title: Velvet Display Case Smudge
evidence.description: Ultraviolet imaging of the display plinth revealed latex glove powder residue along the perimeter seal.
evidence.establishes: The casing was opened using powdered disposable examination gloves.
evidence.reliability_notes: Cornstarch glove lubricant matched conservation lab stock.

redHerrings: Ronald Vance's jumper wire proved electrical tampering, but he was blackmailed into placing it without knowing which case was targeted.
Garrick Cole's presence at 1:58 AM was suspicious, but his body camera audio (E-D) recorded him reporting the vitrine glass already ajar.

hiddenSolution.explanation: Driven by ideological repatriation zeal, Dr. Ramos coordinated with Vance (promising him debt payment) to cut the laser grid at 1:56 AM. She descended into the gallery at 1:57 AM, used her suction lifters to raise the case, took the dagger, and concealed it in her cloth roll before Cole arrived at 1:58 AM to swipe his wand.
decisiveEvidence: Witness statement (Seen in corridor at 1:52 AM with cloth roll)
uncertainties: Whether the Greek repatriation committee had prior knowledge of her theft
hiddenSolution.alternativeExplanation: Garrick Cole lifted the glass at 1:58 AM after Vance disabled the lasers.

missingEvidence: Search of Dr. Ramos's personal locker in the faculty club
rules: A patrol wand swipe can establish arrival right after a theft has taken place.
Technical sabotage (jumper wires) is often commissioned by ideological actors who cannot do the electrical work themselves.
